messages:
support_mike: FYI acme-prod is seeing p99s ~3-4x for embeddings since ~08:12 UTC. Started after the eu-west nodepool rollout this morning. Customers are escalating.
ops-bot: Alert: embed-api.p99 > 4s (service: embeddings, region: eu-west-2) — incident id INC-1767777 — <https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts/1767777|view graphs> :rotating_light:
infra-liz: Which nodepool/instance types? Any repro steps from the customer?
support_mike: Repro is simple — hammer embeddings endpoint with the same payload they use. Example:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"openembed-1","input":"lorem ipsum dolor sit amet"}' 
  -w '\nhttp_code:%{http_code} time_total:%{time_total}'
```
On affected nodes that returns ~6.2s, baseline is ~1.4s.
raj: We rolled CUDA 12.2 driver to eu-west-2 at 07:45 UTC as part of the driver consistency rollout. Could be related.
amy: Also seeing NVMe warnings on a host: dmesg excerpt:
```
[08:15:02] nvme nvme0: I/O timeout, aborting command 0x12
[08:15:02] nvme nvme0: queue 2 timeout, reset controller
```
sre_elena: Please run these quick checks on an impacted host:
1) `iostat -x 1 3`
2) `sudo dmesg | tail -n 40`
3) `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-pmon.csv & sleep 5; pkill -f nvidia-smi`
infra-liz: Pushing small shell probe now to node i-euw2-0a1b2c to collect iostat/dmesg/gpu pmon.
support_mike: iostat snippet from i-euw2-0a1b2c:
```
Device:    rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await  r_await  w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1    0.00  50.00 45.00  0.00  1024  4096    114.67   12.91   68.2   70.1     10.5   2.25  99.00
```
amy: That avgqu-sz and %util look saturated — NVMe queueing causing host-side stalls and pushing token latency up.
jordan: We have a dedicated capacity pool for acme. I can route traffic there temporarily. Want me to roll 10% -> 100%?
raj: Agreed: plan = 1) route customer to dedicated pool 2) rollback CUDA 12.2 on canary nodes 3) run synthetic IO isolation test 4) continue monitoring.
sre_elena: Addendum: don't do kernel boot flags during customer cutover. If rollback of driver reduces p99, we'll schedule kernel tweaks later (nvme parameters, qdisc changes) as postmortem action.
ops-bot: Deploy-bot: starting traffic-shift to dedicated-acme at 1767777200 (10% -> 100% over 3 min).
jordan: Cutover in progress — 25% -> 100% now. Watching p99 and errors.
support_mike: After routing, acme p99 dropped back to ~1.6s at 08:37 UTC. Customer confirms much improved on call.
infra-liz: Rolling driver rollback on canary hosts (i-euw2-0a1b2c, i-euw2-0d3e4f) to CUDA 12.1 packages. If canary stable for 10m, schedule fleet rollback.
amy: Collected dmesg + nvme SMART from affected host shows increased media errors in SMART counters — filing follow-up with hardware team for drive health.
raj: Important to capture: driver package version, kernel version, nvme firmware, node ids, exact timeline. We'll open tracking bug BUG-1767777 and attach repro steps and logs.
support_mike: Customer will keep traffic on dedicated pool until we finish rollback. They asked for ETA; told them we'll update in 2 hours.
ops-bot: Incident state: mitigation in place (routing), severity: sev2, assigned: eng-infra. Next: postmortem and follow-up actions documented in BUG-1767777. :memo:
